questions.stem: Bones of the lower (pelvic) limb, anterior view. Which matches are correct?
questions.explanation: c is the tibia (medial, thick) and d the fibula (lateral, thin). e points to the tarsal bones; the metatarsals are f.

questions.stem: Bones of the lower (pelvic) limb, anterior view. Which matches are correct?
questions.explanation: b is the patella, lying in front of the knee above the tibia.

questions.stem: Constitution of the hip bone (lateral surface). Which matches are correct?
questions.explanation: The ilium (k) forms the upper wing; the pubis (l) is anterior and the ischium (m) posterior-inferior. All three meet at the acetabulum.

questions.stem: Hip bone, lateral surface. Which matches are correct?
questions.explanation: The anterior border is on the right (b, c) and the ischial tuberosity (l) is posterior-inferior. g lies on the pubis, at the anterior-inferior corner.

questions.stem: Bony pelvis, anterior view. Which matches are correct?
questions.explanation: In anterior view we see the inner surface of the ilium: b is the iliac fossa (the gluteal surface is lateral). g is the obturator foramen.

questions.stem: Bony pelvis, anterior view. Which matches are correct?
questions.explanation: d is the anterior superior iliac spine, with the anterior inferior spine (e) below it. h is the pubic symphysis, in the midline in front.

questions.stem: Bony pelvis, anterior view. Label c points to a ridge on the inner surface of the ilium that forms the lateral boundary of the pelvic inlet. It is:
questions.explanation: The arcuate line separates the iliac fossa (greater pelvis) from the lesser pelvis and forms the lateral boundary of the pelvic inlet, with the promontory behind and the symphysis in front.

questions.stem: Femur, anterior and posterior views. Which matches are correct?
questions.explanation: h is the greater trochanter (lateral, above) and m the lesser trochanter (posteromedial, below the neck). The intertrochanteric crest (l) is posterior; the intertrochanteric line (k) anterior.

questions.stem: Femur, anterior and posterior views. Which matches are correct?
questions.explanation: q is the medial epicondyle (on the head side, i.e. medial, in both views). r is the medial condyle seen from behind.

questions.stem: Patella, anterior and posterior views. What does label s point to?
questions.explanation: The base of the patella is its broad upper edge (s); the apex (t) points downward.

questions.stem: Tibia and fibula, anterior and posterior views. Which matches are correct?
questions.explanation: a is the lateral condyle of the tibia (fibula side). i is the medial malleolus of the tibia; j the lateral malleolus at the lower end of the fibula.

questions.stem: Tibia and fibula, anterior and posterior views. Which matches are correct?
options: f → anterior border of the tibia
questions.explanation: g points to the shaft of the tibia in both views; the fibula is the thin lateral bone marked h.

questions.stem: Skeleton of the foot, dorsal view. Which matches are correct?
questions.explanation: k is the navicular (medial, in front of the talus) and j the cuboid (lateral, in front of the calcaneus).

questions.stem: Skeleton of the foot, dorsal view. Which matches are correct?
questions.explanation: The three cuneiforms run medial to lateral: g (medial), h (intermediate), i (lateral). Together with the navicular and cuboid they form the anterior tarsus.

questions.stem: Skeleton of the foot, dorsal view. Which statements are correct?
options: The hallux has only two phalanges (no b)
questions.explanation: c is the proximal phalanx. 1 marks the phalanges, 2 the metatarsals and 3 the tarsus.
